public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Bugeaud Collection of Conjectures and Open Questions: $p$-adic Littlewood Conjecture

This is the $p$-adic analogue of the Littlewood conjecture, posed by de Mathan and
Teulié. A liminf-based formulation also appears in the file
`FormalConjectures/Wikipedia/LittlewoodConjecture.lean` as `padic_littlewood_conjecture`.

*References:*
  - [Bug12] Bugeaud, Yann. "Distribution modulo one and Diophantine approximation."
    Vol. 193. Cambridge University Press, 2012. Chapter 10.
  - [dMT04] de Mathan, Bernard, and Olivier Teulié. "Problèmes diophantiens simultanés."
    Monatshefte für Mathematik 143.3 (2004): 229-245.
  - [EK07] Einsiedler, Manfred, and Dmitry Kleinbock. "Measure rigidity and $p$-adic
    Littlewood-type problems." Compositio Mathematica 143.3 (2007): 689-702.
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace Bugeaud08

/--
Problem 10.8 ($p$-adic Littlewood conjecture). For every real number $\xi$ and
every prime number $p$,
$$\inf_{q \ge 1} q \cdot \lVert q \xi \rVert \cdot |q|_p = 0,$$
where $\lVert \cdot \rVert$ denotes the distance to the nearest integer and
$|\cdot|_p$ denotes the $p$-adic absolute value. Posed by de Mathan and
Teulié [dMT04].
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem problem_10_8 (ξ : ℝ) (p : ℕ) (hp : p.Prime) :
    sInf {x : ℝ | ∃ q : ℕ, 1 ≤ q ∧
      x = q * padicNorm p q * distToNearestInt (q * ξ)} = 0 := by
  sorry

/--
The quadratic case of Problem 10.8. de Mathan and Teulié [dMT04] solved the
$p$-adic Littlewood conjecture for quadratic real numbers.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem problem_10_8.variants.quadratic (ξ : ℝ) (p : ℕ) (hp : p.Prime)
    (hξ : (minpoly ℚ ξ).natDegree = 2) :
    sInf {x : ℝ | ∃ q : ℕ, 1 ≤ q ∧
      x = q * padicNorm p q * distToNearestInt (q * ξ)} = 0 := by
  sorry

/--
The exceptional set for Problem 10.8 has Hausdorff dimension zero (Einsiedler
and Kleinbock [EK07].
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem problem_10_8.variants.exceptional_set_dimH_zero (p : ℕ) (hp : p.Prime) :
    dimH {ξ : ℝ | Filter.atTop.liminf
      (fun q : ℕ ↦ q * padicNorm p q * distToNearestInt (q * ξ)) ≠ 0} = 0 := by
  sorry

end Bugeaud08

reformulations.difference: The exceptional set uses liminf as q tends to infinity being nonzero, rather than the positive-q infimum being positive in Bugeaud’s infimum formulation. The Lean form also matches Einsiedler–Kleinbock’s original statement directly.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Write a(q)=q|q|_p‖qξ‖. These terms are nonnegative. If a positive-index term is zero, qξ is an integer and every positive multiple of that index also gives zero. Otherwise every finite positive-index segment has a positive minimum, so infimum zero forces arbitrarily small terms at arbitrarily large indices. Thus infimum zero is equivalent to liminf zero. Moreover a(p^n)=‖p^nξ‖≤1/2, so the real-valued liminf is finite and its default-value cases cannot intervene. Consequently liminf≠0 is equivalent to infimum>0. This exact equivalence is proved as Review.exceptional_iff in /workspace/review/scratch.lean.

sources_consulted: Yann Bugeaud, Distribution Modulo One and Diophantine Approximation (2012), Problem 10.8, p. 215, and §2.6, pp. 40–41; Google Books search-within excerpts: https://books.google.com/books?jscmd=SearchWithinVolume2&q=%2210.8%22&vid=NeEpoAf7k0IC&start=0 ; https://books.google.com/books?jscmd=SearchWithinVolume2&q=%22Mathan%22&vid=NeEpoAf7k0IC&start=0 ; https://books.google.com/books?jscmd=SearchWithinVolume2&q=%222.34%22&vid=NeEpoAf7k0IC&start=0

Bugeaud’s book page, contents, and reference updates: https://irma.math.unistra.fr/~bugeaud/Book2.html ; https://irma.math.unistra.fr/~bugeaud/travaux/CUPtoc.pdf ; https://irma.math.unistra.fr/~bugeaud/travaux/Biblioajour193.pdf
Bernard de Mathan and Olivier Teulié, Problèmes diophantiens simultanés (2004), publisher abstract: https://doi.org/10.1007/s00605-003-0199-y

Manfred Einsiedler and Dmitry Kleinbock, Measure rigidity and p-adic Littlewood-type problems, §1.1 and Theorem 1.1; LaTeX source: https://arxiv.org/e-print/math/0506514 ; abstract/version record: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0506514

Yann Bugeaud, Around the Littlewood conjecture in Diophantine approximation (2014), §2, particularly the quadratic-case discussion, Conjecture 9, and Theorem 14: https://irma.math.unistra.fr/~bugeaud/travaux/LittBes1.pdf
review.notes: All three declarations checked; no defects found. Lean experiments verified nonemptiness and lower boundedness of the infimum set, the liminf bounds and equivalence above, small p-adic norm values, and nearest-integer boundary cases. The minimal-polynomial hypothesis excludes rational and transcendental inputs and is satisfied by √2. The scratch file compiles successfully, and the equivalence proofs have no sorryAx dependency. The full de Mathan–Teulié paper was inaccessible, but its quadratic result is explicitly confirmed by its publisher abstract, Einsiedler–Kleinbock’s introduction, and Bugeaud’s survey. The open/solved tags agree with the consulted sources.
